content.title: When will DISH channels return? Latest updates on the Gray Media dispute and blackout
content.text: DISH subscribers are still without local channels as Gray Media dispute continues. Find out what to watch now. (AP Photo/Paul Sakuma)ASSOCIATED PRESSIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.DISH Network subscribers across the country remain without key local broadcast channels more than three weeks after a high‑profile carriage dispute with Gray Media triggered a sweeping blackout. The disruption began March 10, 2026, when negotiations between the satellite provider and the station owner broke down just ahead of a contract renewal deadline, resulting in the removal of 226 local stations across 113 markets from DISH’s lineup.The blackout affects local affiliates of nearly every major broadcast network, including ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, The CW, MyNetworkTV and Telemundo, cutting off access to daily local news, severe weather coverage, live sports and popular primetime programming. For many households—especially those without cable or broadband alternatives—the sudden loss has been both disruptive and confusing.How DISH customers can still watch ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC and moreWhile the blackout continues, viewers still have several reliable alternatives for accessing network programming using free and paid streaming options during the dispute:FuboFree trial and up to $30 off your first month203+ channels, along with many local affiliatesStrong sports lineupDIRECTVFive‑day free trial and up to $40 off first month90+ channels depending on planAll major networks available in most marketsSling TV50% off your first monthIncludes FOX and NBC in select markets (Blue plan)Low‑cost, flexible streaming passesDisney+ / Hulu bundleBundle includes Hulu and Disney+ at 46% off individual subscription prices.PeacockAffordable plans start at $7.99/moStreams NBC content, live sports and originalsParamount+Low monthly rate $8.99/moStreams CBS live (on Premium plan)Includes SHOWTIMEWhat’s happening with negotiations?As of April 3, there is still no announced resolution or restoration timeline. Both DISH and Gray Media say they are willing to negotiate, but public statements from each side suggest talks remain stalled. Neither company has filed a formal complaint with the FCC, though industry observers say that option remains on the table if discussions fail to move forward.According to industry analysts, previous disputes involving Gray Media were often resolved quickly. However, this standoff appears more entrenched due to what both sides describe as unprecedented contract demands, raising concerns the blackout could last longer than viewers typically experience.Why the DISH–Gray Media dispute escalatedAt the center of the disagreement that began in early March are retransmission consent fees, which are payments television providers make to broadcast station owners for the right to carry their channels.DISH says Gray Media sought significant fee increases during renewal talks, despite shrinking traditional TV audiences and the growing availability of lower‑cost streaming options. DISH also claims Gray introduced late-stage conditions involving stations Gray does not yet own, leaving little time to finalize a deal. The company says it rejected the proposal to avoid passing higher costs on to subscribers in the form of monthly rate hikes.Gray Media, meanwhile, has accused DISH of insisting on a “materially adverse” contract provision that it says does not appear in any of its hundreds of other distribution agreements. Gray argues that DISH failed to negotiate in good faith under FCC rules.
